q: And euery faire from faire ſome-time declines, \ By chance, or natures changing courſe vntrim'd: \ But thy eternall Sommer ſhall not fade, \ Nor looſe poſſeſſion of that faire thou ow'ſt, \ Nor ſhall death brag thou wandr'ſt in his ſhade, \ When in eternall lines to time thou grow'ſt,
1609, William Shakespeare, “Sonnet 18”, in Shake-speares Sonnets. […], London: By G[eorge] Eld for T[homas] T[horpe] and are to be sold by William Aspley, →OCLC, signature C, verso:
Now don't you wait or hesitate / Let's move before they raise the parking rate, ow!
Then you ran into the bedroom / You were struck down / It was your doom, Annie / Ow!

Improvising a stretcher from a cupboard door, they levered Mrs Dibble on to it and got her upstairs to "Hoos!" and "Ows!" of anguish, and laid her on the bed, where Rita administered another stiff dose of gin.
